titulo: A dog in the car for just a minute with the window cracked
destinatario: se lo manda alguien con perro a su amigo que deja al perro 'un minuto' en el auto mientras entra a la tienda, para decirle que lo lleve con él
regla_guardable: Car in the sun: about 40°F hotter in an hour, most of it in the first 30 minutes. Take your dog with you.
fuentes: Pediatrics (American Academy of Pediatrics), 2005: McLaren, Null and Quinn, Heat Stress From Enclosed Vehicles: Moderate Ambient Temperatures Cause Significant Temperature Rise in Enclosed Vehicles (dark sedan, sunny days, outside highs 72-96 °F, average rise about 40 °F in one hour, about 80% of it in the first 30 minutes; cracked windows did not significantly slow the rise)
AVMA: never leave a pet alone in a parked vehicle

frases.texto: You leave your dog in the car for just a minute, window cracked, and figure it's fine.
But a closed car in the sun heats up fast, and a cracked window barely helps.
A two thousand five Pediatrics study tracked a dark car in the sun for one hour.
On days from seventy-two to ninety-six degrees outside, the inside rose about forty degrees.
And about eighty percent of that rise happened in the first thirty minutes.
Heads up: that was one dark car on sunny days. But a dog locked inside can't leave, and can get heatstroke.
If you're leaving the car, take your dog with you.
Send this to the friend who leaves the dog in the car for a minute.
